editorial:
Imagine being a rich kid who just wants to prove he can make it on his own. That is exactly where you find Jack Newberry. He is tired of relying on his dad's money and decides to dive headfirst into the wild world of early movies. He puts every cent he has into a big project and even borrows a huge sum from his girlfriend's father to make it happen. The whole vibe is lighthearted and funny, focusing on the chaos of trying to build something from scratch when the stakes are incredibly high. You will really root for Jack as he navigates the stress of the film business.

What really makes this one work is the funny dynamic between Jack and the eccentric director he hires, Eric von Greed. The pacing stays snappy, so you never feel bored. While it is a silent film, the physical comedy carries the story perfectly. If you enjoy old-school charm, you should definitely track this down. It is best enjoyed by adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best quality, but you can also look for a high-def digital rental on Apple TV to see those crisp images.
endingExplained: Everything comes together when the movie Jack funded turns out to be a giant hit. Because the film makes so much money, Jack is able to pay back every penny he borrowed from his girlfriend's father. This proves to the old man that Jack is a smart businessman and not just a spoiled rich kid. With his reputation fixed and his pockets full, Jack finally gets the blessing he needs to marry his sweetheart and live happily ever after.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic silent comedies and underdog stories.
